Article Title: 'Who approved pellet guns?' Rahul Gandhi writes Amit Shah over 'barbaric assault' on students
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi along with a victim of alleged pellet gun firing during a students protest

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi wrote to Union home minister Amit Shah , demanding accountability for the "barbaric assault" on students protesting "peacefully" at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on July 20.Calling out the "most shocking" use of "lethal pellet guns," the Congress leader claimed that a 19-year-old student has been undergoing a severe pain and is "likely to lose an eye because he was shot with pellet guns"."Security forces deployed in Delhi answer ultimately to you, so I ask:1. As Home Minister, did you approve the use of lethal force including pellet guns against students? If not, who did? 2. Are the people in plain clothes seen beating students with lathis police personnel or volunteers? Who authorized their deployment?" Rahul Gandhi wrote in a letter addressed to Amit Shah.The Congress leader futher said that it's "government's responsibility to protect protestors and resolve their grievances through dialogue"."Peaceful protest is crucial to any democracy. It is the government's responsibility to protect protestors and resolve their grievances through dialogue. Such brutal violence destroys every norm, and has outraged the country. Youth and students, the future of our country, are demanding answers and accountability.Their voice will be heard," he further wrote.Rahul Gandhi on Saturday slammed the government, saying children protesting for their rights receive "pellets" instead of "justice."In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi shared a video featuring a youth who was reportedly beaten by the Delhi Police during Monday's protests against paper leaks."Sahil was standing with the Tricolour in his hand, merely asking for a clean, fair exam and the fruit of his hard work--the police raised a gun and badly injured him by firing pellets. This is not British tyranny; it is the brutality of the Modi government in independent India--where innocent students demanding their rights receive pellets instead of justice," the post read.More than 118 police personnel sustained injuries, including senior officers holding the ranks of Special Commissioner of Police, Joint Commissioner of Police, Additional Commissioner of Police, Deputy Commissioner of Police, Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police, and Assistant Commissioner of Police, along with several female police personnel. During the scuffle, around 60 protesters were also reported to have been injured.On Friday, the Union Cabinet approved amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, to strengthen the anti-paper leak law amid continuing nationwide protests over the NEET-UG row, while the deadlock in Parliament continued for the fifth day.According to sources, the proposed amendment Bill is likely to be tabled in Parliament on Monday, July 27.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi wrote to Union home minister Amit Shah. He demanded accountability for the "barbaric assault" on students protesting "peacefully" Gandhi said a 19-year-old student is "likely to lose an eye because he was shot with pellet guns"

Article Title: CRPF to do post-analysis of RAF action in NEET protests, says DG; 47 RAF personnel injured
Article Text:
CRPF director general Gyanendra Pratap Singh

NEW DELHI: CRPF director general Gyanendra Pratap Singh on Saturday said the force would conduct a professional post-analysis of the action taken by personnel of Rapid Action Force (RAF), a unit of CRPF, against anti-NEET paper leak protestors, including during the July 20 march to Parliament.“Now, since agitation has been called off, and once assembled people disperse, we would make a professional post-event assessment, like we do after every major assignment, and then let you know of the view of force headquarters,” Singh told TOI on Saturday. This is the first official statement from CRPF in the wake of allegations that pellet guns were used against protestors during the July 20 march to Parliament.Three people have claimed to have suffered pellet injuries in the police action.At least 47 RAF personnel too sustained injuries, allegedly from violent elements in the protests.Sources said the post-event assessment by CRPF will go into all possible aspects of RAF deployment during the protests. This would include action taken by RAF personnel against the protestors, riot-control gear used by them and whether the ground situation justified it. It will examine if the RAF response was graded and in line with the standard operating procedures and riot control manual.An officer said the CRPF will also examine the provocation and aggression that the RAF personnel likely faced at the hands of external, motivated elements who may have infiltrated the protests.CRPF sources said of the 47 RAF personnel injured during the course of their deployment for protests in the Capital, six have sustained head injuries and four, fractures. An officer claimed RAF personnel were hit by protesters with iron rods, likely retrieved from damaged railings. The accounts of the personnel regarding how the injuries were sustained, will be recorded as part of the post-event analysis.Delhi Police had clarified that they do have any pump action guns (PAG), but these are part of RAF’s standard anti-riot gear, along with shock batons. The CRPF review will probe allegations of firing of pellets by any personnel on duty, and if such action was authorised, justified and part of a graded response.NEW DELHIPAG, commonly known as pellet gun, is classified as a 'non-lethal’ anti-riot measure. As per the standard RAF drill, it is to be used only as a second last resort, with police firing being the last. Any RAF anti-riot action should start with engagement with the protestors or unruly mob, followed by warning on public address system to disperse. If all this fails, water cannon or tear gas may be used. Pellet gun is the next level of force applied, and may be fitted with a muzzle deflector so that the pellets hit only the lower body, leaving vital organs unharmed.
Article Summary: CRPF director general Gyanendra Pratap Singh on Saturday said the force would conduct a professional post-analysis of the action taken by personnel of Rapid Action Force. This is the first official statement from CRPF in the wake of allegations that pellet guns were used against protestors during the July 20 march to Parliament.

Article Title: Gen Z outreach: PM Modi asks ministers to shore up presence on Insta
Article Text:
PM Modi on video

NEW DELHI: Buoyed by the response to his midnight post on Instagram Thursday, which got 305 million views, PM Modi Friday returned to the social media platform. "Thank you, friends. I had an opportunity to connect with you late last night. The way you responded to my video post and gave constructive suggestions, thanks to everybody. Your love will continue and our bond will strengthen," the PM said, reports Dipak Dash.His remarks reflected satisfaction, with officials calling it a "successful connect" with Gen Z, who have been wooed by CJP and other opponents. Within minutes, Friday's video had garnered 9.3 million views.This came barely hours after PM urged his Cabinet colleagues to use more of Instagram, saying it will help them stay connected with the youth. He was interacting with them after the Cabinet meeting on Friday. Official sources said PM's choice of Instagram to announce govt's decision to toughen the anti-paper leak law earned him around 1 million new followers.Prime Minister Narendra Modi asked ministers how many of them were actively using social media platforms such as Instagram.He said the platform has been popular with large sections of youth and emphasised using the social networking site to connect with them.PM Modi has been using Instagram since 2014.His advice comes amid a growing sense that BJP, which successfully leveraged mass use of WhatsApp to steal a march over its rivals, runs the risk of ceding the advantage in reaching out to Gen Z, which is not as enamoured of the messaging platform and is more comfortable with the photo & short form video service.PM Modi, a tech enthusiast, has repeatedly urged his ministers to hold interactive sessions with youth on this platform. He has said govt as well as BJP should more active on social media. Chairing the council of ministers meeting in Jan 2023, he had stressed that social media had emerged as the main source of information for large sections of the youth and its growing allure needed to be harnessed.
Article Summary: PM Modi returns to Instagram to thank his followers for their support. His midnight post on Thursday got 305 million views. PM Modi urged Cabinet colleagues to use more of Instagram. He said it will help them stay connected with the youth. His choice of Instagram to announce govt's decision to toughen the anti-paper leak law earned him around 1 million new followers.

Article Title: 'Rewarding corruption': CJP attacks Centre over education secretary's replacement
Article Text:
Education secretary's transfer triggers fresh CJP attack on Centre

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday alleged that the transfer of the Education Secretary amounted to "rewarding corruption instead of ensuring accountability". He claimed that the official had been replaced by an IAS officer from the Animal Husbandry Department who faces "severe multi-crore corruption charges"."Last night, the Education Secretary was transferred. He was replaced by an IAS officer from the Animal Husbandry Department who has severe multi-crore corruption charges against him. The entire crisis around paper leaks and NEET was about systemic corruption," Dipke said in a post on X.Abhijeet further said that replacing one bureaucrat with another facing "serious corruption allegations" was "a direct insult to young people across India".Questioning whether this was the "compromise" the government expected students to accept, he asserted that "this is not accountability" and said the protest would continue until Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns."Replacing one bureaucrat with another facing serious corruption allegations is a direct INSULT to young people across India.Is this the "compromise" the government expects us to accept? This is not accountability. We will not stop until Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns," Dipke added.The Centre on Thursday carried out a major bureaucratic reshuffle, making 13 secretary-level appointments across ministries and departments, including key changes in the education ministry, amid continuing protests over the alleged NEET paper leak.Senior IAS officer Naresh Pal Gangwar has been appointed Secretary, Department of Higher Education, while T K Anil Kumar has been named Secretary, Department of School Education and Literacy. According to an order issued by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC), Gangwar, a 1994-batch IAS officer of the Rajasthan cadre, will succeed Vineet Joshi as Secretary of the Department of Higher Education.The agitation over the NEET paper leak spread across several states on Friday, a day after CJP called for nationwide demonstrations. Protesters condemned the Delhi Police crackdown on July 20 and reiterated their demand for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.As the protests gathered momentum across states, the Congress directed its state units to organise candlelight marches and 'satyagraha' in every district on Saturday evening to protest against the "irregularities in the NEET and CBSE examinations and the subsequent repressive actions by the Modi government".On Friday, a high-level meeting between leaders of CJP and senior BJP leaders, including Union Health Minister JP Nadda and Union Minister Jitendra Singh, was held at the Constitution Club in New Delhi.Earlier, activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike at Medanta Hospital in the presence Nadda and Jitendra Singh after the Union government gave a written assurance on the NEET examination issue and broader systemic reforms to the country's competitive examination framework.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi assured that strict action would be taken against those responsible for the alleged paper leaks. He also said the Union Cabinet would consider a draft Bill proposing fast-track courts and stricter punishment for offenders.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said the transfer amounted to "rewarding corruption instead of ensuring accountability" He claimed that the official had been replaced by an IAS officer from the Animal Husbandry Department who faces "severe multi-crore corruption charges" The Centre on Thursday carried out a major bureaucratic reshuffle.

Article Title: Army rescues 57 stranded as major flood relief operation begins in Gujarat's Navsari
Article Text: The Indian Army on Saturday rescued 57 people stranded by floodwaters at Tata High School on Ring Road in Gujarat's Navsari district as heavy rainfall continued to batter parts of the state. Seperately, Army personnel also evacuated vulnerable residents from Sanduri village in the Madhuban Dam area of Dadra and Nagar Haveli.The rescue operations were launched under the Army's humanitarian assistance and disaster relief initiative following distress calls from flood-hit areas.Responding to an emergency call, southern command deployed rescue teams to Sanduri village, where Army personnel worked in coordination with the civil administration and local volunteers to shift 23 vulnerable civilians to a designated relief shelter.The Army said medical assistance was provided on-site, while essential rations and relief supplies were distributed to residents who remained in the village. It added that relief and rescue operations were continuing across the affected areas.The flooding also disrupted road connectivity in Gujarat. The Ahmedabad district police announced the temporary closure of the Ahmedabad-Viramgam Highway after excessive water flow made the route unsafe."No vehicle from Sanand to Viramgam and Viramgam to Sanand is safe to ply over it. We are closing the entire highway for the time being," the Ahmedabad District Police said, according to news agency ANI.Ahmedabad district collector Bhavya Verma told the news agency that the authorities remained on high alert despite the situation being under control."We have also deployed Indian Army and SDRF teams along the Ahmedabad-Rajkot Highway. The situation is currently under control, though waterlogging persists in several areas. All administrative and rescue teams are actively deployed on the ground. A red alert for heavy rainfall remains in effect for Ahmedabad district tomorrow as well..." Verma told ANI.He said Dholka and Viramgam recorded the highest rainfall in the district over the past 24 hours, adding that rescue operations were being carried out with the assistance of the SDRF, police and the local administration.Meanwhile, Gujarat deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi visited flood-affected areas in Umargam of Valsad district on Friday, where he reviewed the situation, interacted with residents and urged people to avoid rumours and follow official advisories.Earlier this week, the NDRF rescued 67 people, including 25 women and 22 children, from floodwaters in Navsari's Sarikhurad village. In Tapi district, the SDRF rescued 11 stranded villagers, while in Surat more than 4,800 people from urban and rural areas were shifted to relief centres and safer locations as rescue operations continued.
Article Summary: The Indian Army rescued 57 people stranded by floodwaters at Tata High School on Ring Road in Gujarat's Navsari district. Army personnel also evacuated vulnerable residents from Sanduri village in the Madhuban Dam area of Dadra and Nagar Haveli. The flooding also disrupted road connectivity in Gujarat.

Article Title: 3 years on, SIT probe complete in just 10% of Manipur riot cases
Article Text: NEW DELHI: More than three years after Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives, Supreme Court was informed Friday that probes into only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by SITs of state police while CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.Appearing for the CBI, additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the central probe agency had filed chargesheets in 21 cases and closure reports in six, of which three had been accepted. It was continuing investigations into the remaining four cases.Former Maharashtra DGP Dattatray Padsalgikar, who was appointed to oversee the investigations, informed the court through a report that of the 3,020 cases being probed by the SITs across eight districts, chargesheets had been filed in only 301 cases and trial had commenced in 10.The CJI-led bench told the investigators to act expeditiously. Given the volume of cases, SC mulled setting up special courts to try these exclusively. It sought responses to this from Manipur govt and the high courts of Assam and Manipur.SC had transferred investigations into cases of rape-murder other heinous offence to CBI and shifted their trial to Guwahati. The central agency told the court that examination of witnesses residing in Manipur through video-conferencing was a challenge because of law-and-order situations, non-cooperation and language barriers as they spoke different dialects.Senior advocate Ngangom Junior Luwang complained that no effort had been made to trace 30 missing people and without their remains, authorities were not issuing death certificates required for other purposes. SC asked him to approach Manipur high court.Advocate Sharukh Alam submitted that land belonging to churches vandalised during the clashes were getting encroached upon and said govt had taken no steps to reconstruct them. Bhati said govt's priority was to reconstruct damaged dwelling units. The bench said govt was right to prioritise reconstructing houses but asked it to take steps to stop encroachment of places of worship.
Article Summary: Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives. Only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by state police. CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.

Article Title: FIRs against protesters to be quashed, compensation to be given & 5-point Charter: What Centre, CJP said in joint press meet
Article Text:
The joint press conference was attended by Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, along with CJP national spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka and CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das. (PTI image)

What govt said:

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the government response to the NEET paper leak was adequate? Yes, they acted swiftly No, they should have done more 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janata Party on Saturday withdrew its protest against the irregularities in education system including NEET paper leak at Jantar Mantar after the government agreed to its all its demands.In a joint press conference with Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh and the CJP delegation, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said the decision was taken after an understanding that the terms would be implemented within the agreed-upon timeframe."Cockroach Janta Party declares that we withdraw the agitation in good faith, with the understanding that the agreed-upon terms will be executed within the agreed-upon timelines," Das said."All our demands have been accepted, so we request the protesters to withdraw immediately and return home peacefully. We will inform you of our future strategy or any other issues. But we request the protesters to withdraw immediately," he added.Meanwhile, Nadda said the government had accepted the demands presented by the delegation, including that no police action would be taken against the protesters and that compensation would be provided to the families of students who died by suicide, in accordance with the rules and regulations."We had a long conversation today. They brought a written draft in which they made four points about the ongoing cases in agitation. Along with that, we discussed the other two demands: no retaliatory measures should be taken, compensation should be provided, and their five-point charter should be considered," Nadda said."We will provide them with copies of the FIRs, and no action will be taken. The second thing that has been said is that regarding compensation, the government has clearly stated that we also sympathize. We all have said that there will be compensation according to the rules and regulations. Whatever maximum will be possible will be given to them," he added.On the five-point charter presented by the CJP delegation, Nadda said the government would "think deeply" about the suggestions for reforms in the education examination system."This five-point charter, which you gave me, is related to reforms in education examinations. Regarding it, we have to say that we will think deeply about your charter for reforms in education examinations and, after talking to your delegation, we will try to do whatever we can. So these were their demands. I think the government has sympathetically considered all the demands they had made and has also accepted them," he added.The Centre's agreement came a after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned amid nationwide protests over the NEET paper leak.Pradhan said he had stepped down after considering the situation that had developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country, adding that the government had acted swiftly after irregularities in the NEET-UG examination surfaced by handing the probe to the CBI, cancelling the examination and announcing a re-test.Minutes after Pradhan's resignation, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had declared that the protest would continue until the remaining demands were met. He had sought Rs 1 crore compensation for the families of students who died by suicide following the paper leak and action against police personnel over the alleged crackdown on protesters on July 20.However, following three rounds of talks with the Centre, the CJP on Sunday announced that it was withdrawing its 36-day agitation at Jantar Mantar with immediate effect after the government accepted its remaining demands, while also agreeing to consider the party's five-point charter on examination reforms.
Article Summary: The Cockroach Janata Party on Saturday withdrew its protest against the irregularities in education system including NEET paper leak at Jantar Mantar. In a joint press conference with Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh and the CJP delegation, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said the decision was taken after an understanding that terms would be implemented within the agreed-upon timeframe.

Article Title: Kargil lessons shaped Operation Sindoor: Former army chief General VP Malik
Article Text:
Gen V P Malik meeting frontline troops in Kargil in 1999.

CHANDIGARH: Twenty-seven years after leading the Army during the 1999 Kargil War , former Army chief General VP Malik (retd) said the conflict's hard lessons - from equipment shortages and intelligence gaps to the need for self-reliance - transformed India's military capabilities, enabling the precision strikes on Pakistani airfields during last year's Operation Sindoor without crossing the border."The biggest operational lessons were the need to strengthen intelligence, surveillance and achieve 'atmanirbharta (self-reliance)' in military hardware," Gen Malik told TOI in an interview ahead of the 27th anniversary of Kargil Vijay Diwas . Those lessons, he said, shaped India's military preparedness over the next two decades.Citing Operation Sindoor, he pointed to the armed forces' growing reliance on short- and long-range drones for surveillance and precision strikes, along with advanced rockets and missiles."We did not have to enter Pakistani territory when we struck airfields and radar stations, causing major havoc," he said, contrasting it with Kargil.He said indigenous and imported platforms, including BrahMos, Akash and the S-400, were now tested in real-world conditions. Combined with an integrated tri-services command under Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), they have significantly strengthened India's defence capability.Yet, Gen Malik stressed that technology alone could not win wars. "The man behind the gun is always more important. We must look after them," he said.Recalling his visits to the frontlines in Jammu & Kashmir, Gen Malik said the soldiers themselves became a source of strength. "...every six days, I would visit... While morale in Delhi was sometimes anxious or uncertain, not a single soldier ever told me the task was difficult. Every visit replenished my own morale."Reflecting on the reforms that followed the war, Gen Malik said govt constituted Kargil Review Committee, whose key recommendations included creating the CDS position to improve tri-service integration and civil-military coordination. He added that commemorating Vijay Diwas was not only about paying homage to the martyrs but also ensuring the lessons of the conflict continued to guide armed forces.Gen Malik said the valour displayed remained an inspiration for future generations. While the victory involved strategic planning at the highest level, he insisted the credit belonged to the young officers and soldiers who fought at unforgiving heights. "We must also remember the supporting arms and services. People often forget them but military functions like an orchestra during war. When every arm works in harmony, we achieve victory. "Invoking Bhagavad Gita, he said, "The true test of any plan lies in its execution. As written in the Gita: 'Action is superior to knowledge'."
Article Summary: Former Army chief General VP Malik said the conflict's hard lessons transformed India's military capabilities. He said the biggest operational lessons were the need to strengthen intelligence, surveillance and achieve 'atmanirbharta (self- reliance)' in military hardware.

Article Title: Students protest: Gen Z forces DP Change
Article Text:
Protesters at Jantar Mantar celebrate news of Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation

Why BJP chose to cut its losses

NEW DELHI: Dharmendra Pradhan, who earned his early spurs by leading a protest against a Class 12 question paper leak in Odisha in 1996 as an ABVP national secretary, was forced to resign Saturday as Union education minister, in the face of unrelenting protests fuelled by students’ anger over NEET-UG paper leak.Govt conceded to the key demand of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and the opposition as Pradhan sent his resignation to PM Modi, in an unprecedented ouster of a cabinet minister of his govt for over 12 years, marking a political setback to BJP and a rare boost for its rivals.Five-time Karnataka MP and Union minister Pralhad Joshi, who holds several other portfolios, has been given additional charge of education.Jubilant CJP members, led by its founder Abhijeet Dipke, called off their agitation after a third round of talks with Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh.“Democracy wins,” CJP said on X.CJP spokesperson Saurav Das announced withdrawal of protests with immediate effect at a news conference, where both ministers wore a resigned look. Govt has also agreed to provide “honourable” compensation to families of NEET candidates who died by suicide and withdraw FIRs against protesting students in Delhi and other BJP-governed states, he added.The two sides will again meet after four weeks to work on broader reforms in the exam system, CJP said.In a two-page statement, Pradhan said he has quit so that “anti-national forces do not take advantage of the situation” at Jantar Mantar and across the country”. It is not a matter of personal prestige, he said.His statement was addressed to “my young friends”, a nod to Gen Z, who have been the face of CJP-led protests, and left the all-powerful BJP searching for answers to their unconventional onslaught. A govt functionary said largescale participation of youth gave the campaign, which BJP initially saw as sponsored by AAP and Left-aligned groups, an emotive undercurrent, leaving them little choice but to retreat as the protest grew.For a party which rarely makes any concession to rivals on their terms and exudes an air of bold strength rooted in popular endorsement in polls, BJP’s decision to bow to the student protest also reflects the pragmatism it has shown when confronted with street agitation — better to cut losses than let the pain fester into a more serious challenge.In Nov 2021, Modi had announced withdrawal of farm laws in the face of over a yearlong protest by farmers, which was largely confined to Punjab and parts of Haryana and western UP but had remained stubborn. The PM, too, had ascribed the decision to national interest, which observers thought was a reference to the sensitivity of Punjab as a border state.Pradhan’s mention of the stir at Jantar Mantar but no acknowledgement of Congressled opposition’s protest, which has kept Parliament’s monsoon session deadlocked, is seemingly aimed at denying any credit to BJP’s political rivals while conceding to CJP, which is not really an electoral threat.With Rahul Gandhi, too, stepping up his agitation— his surprise demonstration outside Modi’s residence on July 21 was a highlight — so as not to allow CJP, seen closer to its ‘secular’ rival AAP, hog the limelight, Congress is bound to lay claim to the credit. However, BJP has more often than not seen off its challenge without much political damage.There was sympathy in the ranks for Pradhan who, as petroleum minister, rolled out the vote-spinner Ujjwala scheme and stayed engaged with the cadre. He had a stream of visitors — home minister Amit Shah and finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman included.“We had to swallow the bitter pill because there was a real risk of violence breaking out. Any loss of lives would have been blamed on us. Moreover, it was about students and their families,” said a senior minister.The sense of resignation was accompanied by surprise as to why the leadership did not take measures it subsequently took to tackle the discontent: strengthening of the law against paper leaks, eviction of key bureaucrats from education ministry, drastic action against NTA officials, and Pradhan’s resignation.In his statement, Pradhan, 57, who took charge of education ministry in July 2021, emphasised his decades-long commitment to students and education, and said he took responsibility of the fallout of the NEET-UG paper leak from the very first day.The re-exam result was declared on time, and many poor meritorious students made the cut, he said, while blaming those in responsible positions, alikely swipe at Rahul and other key opposition figures, for trying to mislead students.The BJP brass expressed its full backing for Pradhan, a deft politician who has been the choice of Modi and Shah in helming numerous state elections, as he stepped down. BJP president Nitin Nabin credited him for key reforms and lauded him for prioritising larger interests, in keeping with “the highest standards of integrity and selfless service in public life”.
Article Summary: Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union education minister on Saturday. His ouster marks a political setback to BJP and a rare boost for its rivals. CJP members, led by its founder Abhijeet Dipke, called off their agitation.

Article Title: Govt had to bow before collective struggle of youth, says opposition
Article Text:
Opposition react to Pradhan's exit

NEW DELHI: Following Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, opposition parties Saturday said this marked a victory of democracy and said Modi govt had to "bow before the collective struggle" of the country's youth. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said the youth compelled BJP to bow before their pressure, and also started the countdown to its "ouster from power". "The issue is not limited to one minister or one exam, but reflects a larger breakdown of trust among job aspirants who spend years preparing for competitive exams," he said, calling for strict accountability.NCP-SP chief Sharad Pawar said the resignation was a major victory for youth power.Earlier this week, he met the protesting youths at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. He also met PM Modi a day after."I personally met the PM and told him that dialogue was essential in democracy. If dialogue does not take place, it leads to adverse consequences. I urged the PM to depute senior colleagues to hold talks. I had also told protesters that they should go ahead with talks if govt shows willingness to discuss their demands," Pawar said."Couple of rounds of talks took place. Some of the demands of youths were accepted, they were pressing for the minister's resignation," he said.TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee said, "People in power must realise that power of the people is greater than any office or authority. One can love their country deeply without having to love govt of the day."While Sena UBT president Uddhav Thackeray said, "A single cockroach made a dictator bow down", MNS chief Raj Thackeray said, "Gen Z has uprooted govt's hair. And brought it down to earth."The development has restored people's faith in democracy by proving that govts must ultimately listen to people's voice, AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal said.
Article Summary: Opposition parties say resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan is a victory of democracy. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said the youth compelled BJP to bow before their pressure. NCP-SP chief Sharad Pawar said the resignation was a major victory for youth power.

Article Title: Amarnath yatra resumes via Batal after rain-forced halt
Article Text:
The pilgrimage resumed Saturday

JAMMU: The annual Amarnath Yatra resumed Saturday from Jammu after a six-day suspension forced by rain-caused disruptions, with a fresh batch of over 6,269 pilgrims leaving for the Kashmir cave shrine.The batch, 18th since the yatra started July 3, was flagged off in a convoy of 223 vehicles. “In view of inclement weather, authorities permitted movement of pilgrims only through Baltal, while the traditional Pahalgam route remains closed as a precaution,” an official said.The yatra was suspended on July 19 after heavy rainfall, landslides and unfavourable weather across J&K disrupted both routes -- Pahalgam in Anantnag district and Baltal in Ganderbal --leading to the 3,880-metre high Amarnath cave shrine.Officials said the pilgrimage resumed after weather conditions improved and traffic was restored on Jammu-Srinagar National Highway, which had been blocked by landslides and shooting stones, particularly in the Udhampur-Ramban stretch.LG Manoj Sinha had flagged off the first batch of Amarnath pilgrims early this month. Multi-layered protection is in place, with all pilgrim convoys escorted by security forces.The 57-day yatra concludes on Aug 28, coinciding with Raksha Bandhan.Meanwhile, Border Roads Organisation (BRO)has restored connectivity in Rajouri, Poonch and Reasi, the Jammu border districts where incessant rains triggered multiple landslides.Working on a war footing under Project Sampark, BRO launched a swift and coordinated response to ensure uninterrupted movement of security forces and essential supplies in the three rain-affected districts.“Working tirelessly under hazardous conditions, BRO teams successfully removed debris, stabilised vulnerable stretches and restored traffic on the affected routes in the shortest possible time,” Jammu-based defence PRO Lt Col Suneel Bartwal said.According to the officer, the timely restoration underscores BRO’s unwavering dedication to maintaining strategic infrastructure in remote and border areas. “While essential connectivity on all roads has been restored, teams remain deployed to repair damages and ensure seamless movement of traffic,” Col Bartwal said.
Article Summary: The yatra was suspended on July 19 after heavy rainfall, landslides and unfavourable weather across J&K. The 57-day yatra concludes on Aug 28, coinciding with Raksha Bandhan. Multi-layered protection is in place, with all pilgrim convoys escorted by security forces.

Article Title: 'Will take legal action': CJP firm on punishing cops who used excessive force
Article Text:
Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support the legal action against police officers using excessive force during the protest? Yes, definitely No, it's unnecessary 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party leaders on Saturday met Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar after the protest against the NEET paper leak at Jantar Mantar was called off following education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and the fulfilment of the remaining demands.While speaking to reporters after the meeting, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said they had made it clear that the party would take legal action against every official who used excessive force against students during the July 20 march."There was no specific agenda for the meeting... The discussion took place in a very cordial atmosphere. Senior officers, including the Special Commissioner of the Delhi Police, were also present.We made it clear to them that we have resolved to take legal action against every police officer and RAF personnel who was seen in videos or photographs using excessive force, and those who directly struck people on the head, causing head and hand injuries," Das said."We will initiate legal proceedings against all such police and RAF personnel very soon. When the time comes, we will ensure that those officers who fail to uphold law and order and ensure the safety of the people are sent to jail," he added.Meanwhile, Ashutosh Ranka said the party recognises the "consistent cooperation" of the police."It was a good meeting. We discussed everything that has happened over the past few days. What happened on the 20th was very unfortunate. However, we also recognise that there had been consistent cooperation from the Delhi Police," he said."We acknowledged that as well. We hope this marks the beginning of a new chapter. All our demands have been accepted, including the withdrawal of the FIRs and the assurance that no new FIRs will be filed. All's well that ends well, and we sincerely thank the youth of this country," he added.This comes after the Cockroach Janata Party called off its 36-day agitation following Pradhan's resignation and the government's acceptance of its remaining demands.The CJP declared that it was withdrawing its agitation after the government agreed to all its remaining demands, including compensation for the families of students who allegedly died by suicide following the NEET paper leak and the withdrawal of FIRs against protesters.The announcement came after the third round of talks between the two sides at the Constitution Club of India, where Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh met CJP representatives Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka.Addressing a joint press conference with the CJP leadership, Nadda said the government would provide "honourable compensation," in accordance with the rules, to the families of students who died by suicide following the NEET examination controversy and ensure the withdrawal of all FIRs registered against protesters.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janata Party leaders met Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar on Saturday. They made it clear that they would take legal action against every official who used excessive force during the July 20 march. Article Title: 'Big win for democracy': Arvind Kejriwal congratulates youth on Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation

Article Title: 'Serious charges': Court rejects retired judge Giribala Singh's bail plea in Twisha Sharma case
Article Text:
Twisha Sharma death case (File Photo)

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: A special court in Bhopal on Saturday rejected the bail plea of retired judge Giribala Singh, an accused in the alleged dowry death of former model and actor Twisha Sharma, observing that the charges against her were "serious. "Giribala Singh, Twisha's mother-in-law, is accused in the case after the former model and actor was allegedly found hanging at her marital home in Bhopal on May 12.The retired judge and her son, Samarth Singh, were later arrested on charges of dowry-related harassment, mental abuse and domestic violence. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is probing the case.The bail application was initially listed before Special Judge Neelam Shukla, who recused herself from hearing the matter.The case was then transferred to Special Judge Ram Pratap Mishra, who reserved the order on Friday after hearing arguments from both sides.Seeking bail on humanitarian grounds, the defence argued that Singh, an elderly woman with health issues, was not receiving adequate medical care in jail. It also submitted that her nearly 100-year-old mother depended on her for care.The defence further contended that Singh had cooperated with the investigation, suffered a burglary at her residence while in custody, and received a regular salary and a war widow's pension, making the allegation of dowry demand implausible.Opposing the plea, the CBI argued that Singh's gender alone could not justify bail, particularly when the deceased was also a woman. It pointed out that the Madhya Pradesh High Court had on May 27 quashed the anticipatory bail granted to her by a subordinate court in Bhopal.The agency also alleged that Singh had refused to provide her voice sample during the investigation, attempted to influence the probe by contacting a CCTV technician and a salon operator linked to the case, and sent a private representative to obtain CCTV footage.The CBI argued that her release could enable her to influence witnesses, tamper with evidence or hamper the ongoing investigation.After hearing both sides, the special court rejected Singh's bail application.
Article Summary: Giribala Singh, Twisha's mother-in-law, is accused in the case after the former model and actor was allegedly found hanging at her marital home in Bhopal on May 12. The retired judge and her son, Samarth Singh, were later arrested on charges of dowry-related harassment, mental abuse and domestic violence.

Article Title: 'Goons and their future generations will remember': Bengal invokes 'Goonda Act' over NEET protest violence in first use of law
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The West Bengal government on Saturday invoked its newly enacted "Goonda Act" against those accused of orchestrating violence during Friday's NEET protest, marking the first use of the legislation since it was passed by the state assembly.The West Bengal Public Safety and Control of Anti-social Activities Act, 2026, was passed by the assembly recently after a stormy debate and criticised by the opposition as draconian.Governor RN Ravi approved the legislation earlier this week.Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari announced the move on Saturday."I condemn the attack on our journalist friends on behalf of the entire House. An attack on journalists is unacceptable.We will take such action under the Goonda Act that these goons and even their next three generations will remember it. This is precisely why this law was enacted," Adhikari said in the assembly.He informed the House that around 70 people identified from the Dharmatala rally were "not students" and had no connection with the agitation over the NEET paper leak.Seven FIRs were registered over Friday's violence — six at Hare Street police station and one at Entally police station — with provisions of the new law incorporated into the cases, he told the House."The police exercised maximum restraint despite repeated provocation. That was the clear instruction given to them. They did not fall into the trap," Adhikari said.The chief minister alleged that the rally initially proceeded peacefully before "anti-social elements" entered from behind and attempted to trigger violence.According to him, the protest was organised under the banner of the "United Cockroach March", announced by what he described as a self-proclaimed member of the CJP, with participation from Left and ultra-Left student organisations, including the SFI, DSO, DYSA and AISF."In a democracy, everyone has the right to protest peacefully within the framework of law. The police were specifically instructed not to act unless the situation went completely out of control," he added.Adhikari alleged that as the procession reached Dorina Crossing at Esplanade, shoes and water bottles were hurled first at policemen and then at journalists covering the demonstration."They wanted the police to resort to lathi-charge and tear gas. They wanted a spectacle. But Kolkata Police did not provide them that opportunity. The restraint shown by the force deserves appreciation," he stated.

Article Title: NEET protests, CBI probe, political pressure: Key events that led to Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
Article Text:
Key events that led to Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation

Here are the key events that led to the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan:

Leak sparks outrage

CBI widens probe

Protest movement grows

Centre shifts strategy

Talks remain deadlocked

Opposition steps up pressure

Courts and Parliament

What the resignation means

NEW DELHI: Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on Saturday as Union education minister, taking moral responsibility for the NEET-UG paper leak controversy that has shaken the country's examination system, sparked mass student protests and triggered political confrontations.In his resignation letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Pradhan said he had dedicated more than four decades to students, teachers and education reform.He said the government had acted immediately after irregularities surfaced in the NEET-UG examination held on May 3, including cancelling the test, ordering a CBI probe and deciding to hold a fresh examination. He also said the test would be conducted in computer-based mode from next year.Pradhan said that he had tried from the first day to ensure that no meritorious student suffered because of what he described as an examination mafia. He said the unrest at Jantar Mantar and across the country had saddened him and that he was resigning to prevent anti-national forces from exploiting the situation and to protect the unity of the country.Also Read | Dharmendra Pradhan resigns as Union education minister amid massive student protests The Odisha-born BJP leader had served as education minister since 2021 and was reappointed after the BJP’s victory in the 2024 Lok Sabha election.Cockroach Janta Party chief spokesperson Saurav Das said the party had been called for third round of talks and would stay until a written commitment was made. He described the expected outcome as a 'huge victory'.The crisis began after allegations of a paper leak in the NEET-UG 2026 examination, which was held on May 3. Investigators later said a question set described as a 'guess paper' had circulated among students weeks before the test and that many questions closely matched the actual paper.The National Testing Agency cancelled the exam on May 12 and the government referred the case to the Central Bureau of Investigation for a full probe. The exam, which is used for admission to undergraduate medical and dental courses, had been taken by nearly 22.79 lakh students. The cancellation marked the first full scrapping of NEET in its 13-year history.Also Read | Watch: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke falls on stage after being told Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned The government later announced that the re-examination would be held on June 21 and that no fresh registration would be required. It also said fees already paid would be refunded and that the exam would be shifted to online mode from 2027.The CBI widened its investigation rapidly, carrying out searches at dozens of locations across several states and tracing the alleged source of leaked Physics, Chemistry and Biology questions. The agency said it had identified a network of accused persons, coaching links and middlemen involved in circulating the questions.Among those arrested were a Latur-based doctor, Dr Manoj Shirure and a Pune-based physics faculty member, Tejas Harshadkumar Shah. Investigators said Dr Shirure helped three students access leaked Chemistry questions, while Shah allegedly passed on Physics questions obtained from another accused already in custody.Earlier, the CBI had also arrested a Chemistry lecturer, PV Kulkarni, whom it described as a key figure in the leak. The agency said he had conducted special coaching sessions at his residence in Pune, where questions and answers were dictated and later matched the actual NEET paper.The exam controversy soon became a major student movement. The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ), a satirical youth-led campaign, began protests at Jantar Mantar on June 20, demanding Pradhan’s resignation and accountability over paper leaks and other examination irregularities.The agitation gathered pace after climate activist Sonam Wangchuk joined the protest and began an indefinite hunger strike. His deteriorating health drew wide attention on social media and his later hospitalisation further fuelled public anger. He eventually ended his 26-day hunger strike after receiving written assurances from the government.The CJP said the movement would continue until Pradhan resigned. Its leaders also demanded compensation for the families of students who died by suicide, withdrawal of FIRs against peaceful protesters and a written guarantee that no such cases would be filed in future.The Centre’s response changed over time. At first, several BJP leaders dismissed the protests, but the government later opened negotiations and announced a series of measures to calm the situation.PM Modi said paper leaks were not an ordinary matter and announced fast-track courts to ensure swift punishment for those involved. He also said the government had acted to make sure that nearly 22 lakh students did not lose an academic year.The Union Cabinet later approved amendments to anti-paper-leak law, proposing a maximum jail term of 10 years, a fine of up to Rs 10 crore and a higher minimum sentence. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said the Bill would be brought to Parliament soon.At the same time, the National Testing Agency began a major internal overhaul, terminating 47 officials and recruiting new personnel in cybersecurity, digital forensics and test-centre operations. Officials said the changes were aimed at restoring confidence and tightening examination security.Even as the government expanded its response, its talks with the CJP remained unresolved. A second round of discussions between Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh and CJP representatives ended without a breakthrough. The CJP said the Centre had sought time until Saturday afternoon to respond to its main demand for Pradhan’s resignation.The group said the other two major demandscompensation for bereaved families and withdrawal of cases against peaceful protesters had been accepted in principle. But it insisted that any further meeting must be held at a neutral venue, such as the Constitution Club of India, rather than a minister’s residence.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi renewed his attack on the government, accusing Pradhan of presiding over a collapse of the education system. He also joined opposition leaders in paying tribute to students who died by suicide over the controversy and accused the Centre of using force against peaceful demonstrators.As protests spread across the country, opposition parties intensified their demand for Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, accusing the Centre of failing to protect the integrity of competitive examinations.Parliament witnessed repeated disruptions as INDIA bloc MPs insisted that the education minister step down before any discussion on the NEET controversy could begin.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi emerged as one of the strongest critics of the government, calling Pradhan 'a symbol of the collapse of our education system' and saying, "He has to go." He also said students were making three key demands: the education minister's removal, action against those responsible for the alleged pellet gun use and lathi-charge on protesters, and an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the affected youth.The opposition also organised protests and candlelight marches in solidarity with students and families affected by the alleged paper leak and exam-related suicides.Rahul Gandhi later brought before the media a protester whom he claimed had suffered pellet gun injuries during the Jantar Mantar demonstration, alleging that the government had falsely denied using pellet guns against protesters. "His eye has suffered damage, and he has lost his vision," Gandhi said, while accusing the Centre of attacking the future of the country's youth instead of addressing their concerns.The Supreme Court agreed to hear petitions over alleged excessive police action against protesters. The court also clarified that reports saying it had refused to hear the matter were false.Parliament too was paralysed repeatedly as opposition MPs pressed for Pradhan’s resignation before any debate could begin. The government said it was ready for discussion without preconditions and accused the opposition of blocking parliamentary proceedings.Meanwhile, Delhi Police warned that those directly involved in violence during the protests could face passport cancellation. The warning came after clashes near Jantar Mantar left several police personnel and protesters injured.Pradhan’s resignation is the biggest political consequence so far of the NEET controversy. It follows weeks of criticism over repeated exam irregularities, the handling of protests and the government’s initial response, which opponents said was too slow and dismissive.The CBI probe into the alleged leak has widened across several states, with arrests made and searches carried out in multiple cities. The case has also prompted the government to push a tougher anti-paper leak law, while the National Testing Agency has begun a major overhaul of its staffing and security arrangements.
Article Summary: Dharmendra Pradhan resigns as Union education minister amid massive student protests. The crisis began after allegations of a paper leak in the NEET-UG 2026 examination, held on May 3. Investigators later said a question set described as a 'guess paper' had circulated among students weeks before the test and that many questions closely matched the actual paper.

Article Title: 'First it hurt me, later I took advantage': FM Nirmala Sitharaman's paper leak remarks spark political row
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has come under fire over her remarks on the NEET paper leak controversy after she said some students had used the additional time before the re-examination to improve their performance. The remarks drew sharp criticism from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and Opposition leaders, who accused her of being "insensitive" to students impacted by the alleged leaks.Speaking to news agency ANI, Sitharaman defended the government's handling of the paper leak controversy, saying its response had ensured timely arrests, re-examinations and declaration of results.Sitharaman said the government's response included timely arrests, a re-examination and prompt declaration of results. She said some students had used the additional preparation time to improve their performance, adding, "First it sort of hurt me when the paper leakages happened but later I took advantage of that and prepared even more and my performance has improved and I've done well." She added that such students had "taken this challenge and faced this, and come out bright in bright colours," while asserting that "the government is responding, PM is responding.Sitharaman also accused the Congress of disrupting Parliament despite the government's willingness to discuss the issue.The FM also accused the Congress of disrupting Parliament despite the government's willingness to hold a discussion on the issue. She said the government had agreed to the Opposition's demand for a debate, but the opposition keeps disrupting the house. "The government is willing to have full-fledged discussion in the House, come discuss," she said, accusing the Congress of "disruption of the House" because "the truth will come out, and the government's actions will be placed before the House. They don't want a fair discussion."The remarks come as thousands of students have been protesting for weeks over the alleged NEET paper leaks, with demonstrations centred at Delhi's Jantar Mantar and echoed in several parts of the country. On July 20, protesters marching towards Parliament were lathi-charged and tear-gassed by police and the rapid action force, leaving several students as well as security personnel injured.The government has since reached out to protesters, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi promising strict action against those responsible for paper leaks and Union ministers holding talks with activist Sonam Wangchuk and the representatives of the Cockroach Janta Party.The CJP strongly objected to Sitharaman's remarks, arguing that they trivialised the impact of the controversy on students.The remarks also triggered widespread reactions on social media, with several users criticising Sitharaman's comments as 'deeply insensitive', while accusing the government of downplaying the impact of the paper leak controversy on students.Reacting to her statement, CJP leader Ashutosh Ranka said, "By this logic, every paper in this country should get leaked."In a post on X, the organisation's official handle wrote, "The Finance Minister is claiming NEET students took advantage of the paper leak and worked harder for the re-NEET.Now we're extolling the virtues of paper leaks? This is a shockingly insensitive comment when 20 students have died by suicide because of YOUR incompetence! Shame."The remarks also drew sharp reactions from Opposition leaders. Congress leader Supriya Shrinate took a swipe at Sitharaman, asking her to "please list the benefits" for the 22 students who allegedly died by suicide following the paper leak controversy.Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra also reacted on X, writing, "Honestly this entire Cabinet should resign."

She said some students had used the additional time before the re-examination to improve their performance. The remarks drew sharp criticism from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and Opposition leaders, who accused her of being "insensitive"

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi on Friday launched a sharp attack on the Narendra Modi government, accusing it of responding to students' demands for accountability and education reforms with "cowardice and wanton cruelty" instead of meaningful action.She described July 20, 2026, as "a day of infamy", alleging that the Delhi Police and Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) used lathis and tear gas to disperse peaceful demonstrators. She also claimed that many protesters were injured and that even students returning home were allegedly beaten.Sonia Gandhi alleged that numerous peaceful protesters were injured, and even students heading home were not spared, as police used batons indiscriminately."The nation has seen some of the most depressing visuals of youth whose bodies have been scarred by pellets, the use of which would undoubtedly have been approved by Union home minister Amit Shah himself," the ex-Congress chief wrote in an article titled 'An education system's collapse, young India's trauma', published in The Hindu.Gandhi said the government's handling of the ongoing student protests reflected its unwillingness to engage with the concerns of young people."The videos from that day are seared into our memories and have stirred our collective conscience. Only the government and its captive media are spinning stories around this spontaneous rising tide of protest. It is time to say loud and clear: Stop, these are our sons and daughters, our young men and women," Gandhi said.She said students across the country had been demanding accountability over examination paper leaks and broader reforms in the education system, but alleged that the Centre had chosen repression over dialogue."The student protests are a natural consequence of these interrelated forces: today's bleak education landscape, which evokes only hopelessness, and the Modi government's trademark arrogance and unwillingness to be accountable or constructive," Gandhi wrote.She further alleged that the government had weakened India's education system while acting with "utter impunity, supreme self-delusion, and abject insensitivity".According to Gandhi, it was the moral, political and constitutional responsibility of every public representative to stand with students and protect their future.Referring to the police action against protesters, she claimed the use of force was consistent with the government's previous response to public demonstrations."We all remember vividly how armed policemen and paramilitary forces ravaged university campuses during the Citizenship (Amendment) Act-National Register of Citizens protests in 2020. The unacceptable excesses against India's women wrestlers can never be erased from our memories," she said.Gandhi also criticised the police action during the recent protests over the alleged NEET paper leak and the state of the education system."Their demands have been straightforward and to the point: accountability from the Government of India and education reform. The Narendra Modi government has responded to their courage with cowardice and wanton cruelty, treating them not as inheritors of the future but as enemies of the nation," she said.Sonia's remarks came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that the Union Cabinet would discuss a Bill to strengthen the existing anti-cheating law with stricter penalties for those involved in examination paper leaks.In a recorded message released late on Thursday night, the Prime Minister said the proposed legislation would include provisions for fast-track courts and tougher punishment for offenders. He said the Bill would be finalised after Cabinet approval and introduced in Parliament when the second week of the Monsoon Session begins.Modi said the government had been working for the past two and a half months to address concerns arising from the alleged NEET paper leak. He added that the Centre had ensured that nearly 22 lakh students did not lose an academic year by conducting the re-examination and declaring the results.The Prime Minister's announcement came shortly after the government replaced the Education Secretary amid the continuing protests over the alleged paper leak.Amid ongoing protests, the government named animal husbandry secretary Naresh Pal Gangwar the new secretary for higher education, while TK Anil Kumar the new school education secretary. Incumbent Vineet Joshi, who had charge of both, moved to low-profile panchayati raj department.Officials said the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) had remained in close touch with the education ministry over issues related to the NEET re-test and the implementation of recommendations made by the K Radhakrishnan Committee on reforms to the National Testing Agency (NTA).

Article Title: Low-key Nadda emerges as govt point man in talks with protesters
Article Text:
Nadda emerges as key negotiator from govt's side

NEW DELHI: As the govt's main interlocutor with students protesting under the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) banner, Union health minister JP Nadda has been thrust into the limelight, holding talks with them and visiting the injured in hospitals.This is an interesting turn in Nadda's journey. The former BJP president is not really known for revelling in the spotlight and is more at ease in closed-door political meetings than being in the middle of public attention. That his comments rarely stoke any controversy or ruffle others is being considered an asset when govt is holding talks with a group which is riding the angst of the student community, as any misstep may inflame passions.Nadda cut his teeth in students' politics as an ABVP activist in Patna and Himachal University and grew in the role to head Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha, the youth wing of BJP, collecting long experience of agitational politics, the second nature of student activism, which makes him the right person for the job.BJP circles are of the view that while being health minister who looked after the treatment of injured protesters put Nadda in a position to connect with CJP, his emergence as a negotiator came as a surprise.It is surmised that the former BJP chief's low-key presence added to his acceptability. A BJP functionary said one of his strengths was that he was soft-spoken but also knew where to draw the line, a trait that ensures that he could engage with protestors skilfully while ensuring that the govt's views were also put across firmly.He had also met activist Sonam Wangchuk in a private hospital as part of govt's efforts to persuade him to break his hunger strike and engage in talks to end the stir.Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, known for his political savvy and proven track record of successful political outreach, could have been the other choice but for the fact that his resignation is CJP's main demand.With some other leading BJP figures not really a good fit for the job because of their seniority, the task fell on Nadda, now a member of the party's brains trust.
Article Summary: Nadda cut his teeth in students' politics as an ABVP activist in Patna and Himachal University. He grew in the role to head Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha, the youth wing of BJP. It is surmised that the former BJP chief's low-key presence added to his acceptability.

NEW DELHI: Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Friday night released a video on YouTube describing events from the past few days and sharing footage from the time he was leaving Safdarjung Hospital after the Delhi high court permitted his transfer to Medanta Hospital in Gurgaon.The Safdarjung Hospital administration, however, said the video was recorded before it had received the written order of the high court, according to news agency PTI.Wangchuk was shifted to Safdarjung Hospital by Delhi Police on July 18 from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest site at Jantar Mantar, where he had been on a hunger strike since June 28 in support of the CJP's demands, including accountability for examination paper leaks and the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.Following directions from the Delhi high court, he was moved to Medanta Hospital on July 21.In the video, Wangchuk is seen arguing with a security personnel at Safdarjung Hospital, alleging that he was being stopped from leaving the premises.He can be heard saying that the authorities should either arrest him or allow him to leave.“You are harassing me... Article Summary: Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Friday night released a video on YouTube describing events from the past few days.
