Article Title: 10 killed, nearly 100 injured in Russian strike on Ukraine defence event
Article Text:
Addressing the nation, Zelenskyy blamed Russia for the attack.

At least 10 people were killed and nearly 100 injured after a Russian ballistic missile struck a defence industry event in Ukraine's Kyiv region on Friday, prompting President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to criticise the decision to hold such a gathering during wartime.Ukraine's Emergency Services said rescue operations at the site, located north of the capital, had been completed. Images released by the agency showed emergency workers searching through piles of rubble near several residential houses.Addressing the nation, Zelenskyy blamed Russia for the attack but also questioned the decision to organise a defence-related exhibition while the war continues."Of course, the cause of this attack is Russian missiles, nothing but Russian terror," he said, according to news agency Reuters."However, we have said a thousand times that under these wartime conditions, with such an enemy, it is absolutely unacceptable to hold any weapons exhibitions with large crowds of people, especially near residential buildings."The event, organised by a drone manufacturers' association, was being held a short distance from the outskirts of Kyiv. A spokesperson for Ukraine's General Staff said the venue did not fall under the military's jurisdiction, but stressed that any such event should have been conducted with "maximum security measures".Kyiv regional acting governor Ruslan Oliynyk announced that Saturday would be observed as a day of mourning following the strike.The Ukrainian Council of Defence Industry confirmed that representatives of the country's defence sector were present when the missile hit, but said it had not organised the event.Valerii Borovyk, founder of Ukrainian drone company First Contact, told local media that the missile struck a training ground where the exhibition was taking place.Ukraine's Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko said a criminal investigation had been launched to examine whether officials failed in their duties while organising and conducting the event.Russia also carried out attacks in several other parts of Ukraine on Friday. In the eastern city of Sloviansk, a Russian aerial bomb killed five people and injured nine, according to regional governor Vadym Filashkin. He later said another evening strike on the city injured 16 more people and damaged residential buildings.In the northern Sumy region, a Russian drone attack killed two people, regional governor Oleh Hryhorov said.Meanwhile, in the south-eastern city of Zaporizhzhia, a Russian strike set a shopping centre on fire and injured several people.Russia and Ukraine have repeatedly accused each other of targeting civilians since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, although both sides deny deliberately attacking civilian populations.
Article Summary: At least 10 people killed and nearly 100 injured after a Russian ballistic missile struck a defence industry event in Ukraine's Kyiv region on Friday. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed Russia for the attack but also questioned the decision to organise a defence-related exhibition.

Article Title: Maharashtra TET paper leak: Main accused Bijendra Gupta arrested from Bihar
Article Text:
Maharashtra Police have arrested alleged TET paper leak mastermind Bijendra Gupta (File Photo).





BHIWANDI: The Thane police probing the alleged Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) paper leak case achieved a major breakthrough on Saturday by arresting the alleged mastermind, Bijendra Gupta, after a three-week manhunt. Gupta was apprehended in Bihar along with his associate, Indrajit Singh, taking the total number of arrests in the case to 14.Bijendra is said to be involved in many papers leaks across several states in the country and was arrested earlier but was on bail during which he leaked again TET paper.A police team tracked down the duo during an early morning operation in Bihar and is bringing them to Mumbai. Both accused are expected to be produced before a Bhiwandi court later in the day to seek their custodial interrogation.Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone II) Pawan Bansod confirmed the arrests to TOI. "Our team had been relentlessly searching for Bijendra Gupta for the past three weeks. We succeeded in arresting him this morning. Along with him, one of his associates, Indrajit Singh, has also been arrested. Both accused are being brought to Mumbai and will be produced before the Bhiwandi court," Bansod said.The case came to light after DCP Bansod received a tip-off a day before the June 28 TET examination that a group was arriving in Bhiwandi to sell leaked question papers.Acting on the information, Kongaon police station team laid a trap and arrested three persons allegedly attempting to sell the leaked papers. The subsequent investigation uncovered a well-organised racket involved in leaking examination papers and facilitating unfair means for candidates.The probe has so far revealed a network allegedly operating across multiple states. During the investigation, police arrested several key accused, including two employees of an Agra-based printing press from where Gupta is suspected to have procured the leaked question papers.Among those arrested earlier is Gupta's wife, Suman Gupta, who was traced to Samastipur in Bihar. Investigators believe she played an active role in the financial transactions and logistical support of the alleged racket. Police have also seized multiple electronic devices, documents and financial records during the investigation.Investigators further revealed that Gupta had allegedly finalised a deal through arrested accused Kapil Dahiya to sell the leaked question papers to a Pune resident, who remains absconding and is the only accused yet to be arrested in the case.Police claim the Pune-based suspect was in contact with nearly 50 teacher aspirants who were willing to purchase the leaked question papers before the examination.Officials said Gupta's arrest is expected to provide crucial leads on the exact source of the leaked papers, the money trail and the possible involvement of additional members of the syndicate.
Article Summary: Bijendra Gupta was apprehended in Bihar along with his associate, Indrajit Singh, taking the total number of arrests in the case to 14. Bijendra is said to be involved in many papers leaks across several states in the country and was arrested earlier but was on bail during which he leaked again TET paper.

Article Title: Govt fact-checks viral AI deepfakes of PM, ministers; points to Pakistani handles
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The government has debunked doctored videos circulating on social media that wrongly showed Prime Minister Narendra Modi making threatening remarks against those protesting at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar over perpetual NEET paper leak. The Press Information Bureau (PIB) fact check unit said the clips were AI-generated deepfakes and did not reflect the Prime Minister’s actual statements.In related fact-checks, the government also flagged manipulated videos of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and commerce minister Piyush Goyal that were circulating on social media, falsely portraying them as making similar remarks against protesting students.In a post on X, the PIB fact check unit said, “Pakistani propaganda accounts are circulating a video of Prime Minister @narendramodi featuring fabricated statements that he never made regarding the protest in Delhi.”It added, “#PIBFactCheck: This is an '#AI-generated deepfake video' shared to mislead the public. Prime Minister Narendra Modi did NOT make any such statement.”The fact-check unit said the original video shared by PM Modi had been digitally altered to create a misleading version.It further shared a link to the original, unedited video posted by the PM.The fake video circulating online showed an altered audio track in which PM Modi was allegedly made to say, "We are warning people against participating in the Cockroach Janata Party protest. Those who defy this warning will face strict action from the Government of India to ensure that such behaviour is not repeated in the future. Students are advised to focus on their education, failing which they will be compelled to face serious consequences. We are issuing a clear warning to the students."The original video, posted by PM on his official social media account on Thursday, has since garnered 334 million views on Instagram. In the video, PM Modi addressed viewers as “Friends” and spoke directly into what appeared to be a phone’s front camera, held at arm’s length, with no podium, studio setup or formal backdrop.In the video, the PM said the paper leak issue had caused difficulties for lakhs of students and their parents. He said those responsible had been arrested and that steps were being taken to ensure students did not lose an academic year.The Prime Minister also said provisions for fast-track courts had been prepared and would be taken up by the Union cabinet.The fact check unit also debunked another AI-generated video that falsely showed the PM similar remarks about the cockroach janata party protests. In this manipulated clip, Modi appeared to say, “What is the problem with these cockroaches? Even if one paper gets leaked, what is the big deal? Students can simply appear for the examination again next year.” The PIB clarified that the remarks were fabricated and shared the original video, which showed the Prime Minister speaking about the monsoon and the ongoing Monsoon session of parliament.Additionally, the PIB flagged another digitally altered video of Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan that falsely portrayed him threatening protesting students. The manipulated clip appeared to show Pradhan saying that “big leaders do not resign because of these cockroaches; they crush them under their shoes and throw them into dirty drains where they belong” and warning that protesters would “soon face grave consequences”. Refuting the claims, the PIB said, “Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan did not make any such statement.”The fact-check unit blamed Pakistani propaganda accounts for circulating the digitally altered video containing fabricated claims. The original video was posted on the occasion of Sital Sasthi and made no reference to the protests.The manipulated clip surfaced amid continuing protests led by the CJP, which has consistently demanded that Pradhan be held accountable for the alleged NEET paper leaks and has called for the education minister's resignation as one of its principal demands.In another fact check, the government flagged a separate manipulated video involving commerce minister Piyush Goyal, which falsely claimed that Goyal had made similar threatening remarks against Jantar Mantar protests.The PIB said, “Mr Goyal has made no such statement regarding the protests.”The government urged people to verify the authenticity of videos and rely on official sources before sharing them.
Article Summary: The government has debunked doctored videos circulating on social media that wrongly showed Prime Minister Narendra Modi making threatening remarks. The Press Information Bureau (PIB) fact check unit said the clips were AI-generated deepfakes. The government also flagged manipulated videos of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and commerce minister Piyush Goyal.

Article Title: Delhi Police claims only 3,000 cops present for 10,000 protesters, file 15 FIRs
Article Text:
Delhi police uses facial recognition system at Jantar Mantar

NEW DELHI: Amid the ongoing student protest, Delhi police have deployed around 3,000 police personnel to maintain law and order for nearly 10,000 people present in and around Jantar Mantar.Police sources said around 130 police personnel have been injured and 15 FIRs have been registered in connection with the agitation, according to Delhi Police sources. The police also said around 65 students sustained injuries during the demonstrations.The Delhi Police further said it is using Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras to identify "anti-social elements" visiting Jantar Mantar.According to police sources, more than 2,000 people with criminal records who had visited the protest site have been identified so far, as cited by ANI.This is not the first time the Delhi Police has deployed Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras.The force has previously used the technology as part of security arrangements during Republic Day, Independence Day, Holi, Diwali, Eid, Ramlila celebrations and several other major public events across the city.Meanwhile, Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday said he has been diagnosed with typhoid but asserted that the nationwide protests demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan would continue without interruption.On Friday, Dipke welcomed activist Sonam Wangchuk's decision to end his 26-day hunger strike but reiterated that the movement would continue until its demand for accountability over the examination irregularities is met."Our demonstration will go on until Dharmendra Pradhan steps down. Any meeting must take place at a neutral location or venue. Nothing less than the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan will be accepted," he said.Meanwhile, activist Sonam Wangchuk responded to criticism over his decision to end his 26-day hunger strike held in support of students protesting the alleged NEET paper leak.In a video message shared on social media, Wangchuk questioned why his commitment to the cause required a "character certificate".Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike after receiving a written assurance from the Union government on the NEET examination issue and broader systemic reforms to the country's competitive examination framework.The activist said he had earlier been offered verbal assurances but insisted on a written commitment, which delayed the end of his fast by two days.Following a nearly two-hour meeting with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, representatives of CJP said the government had sought time until Saturday afternoon to consider their demand for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
Article Summary: Delhi police deploy 3,000 police personnel to maintain law and order at Jantar Mantar. Police sources say around 130 police personnel have been injured and 15 FIRs have been registered. Delhi Police is using Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras to identify "anti-social elements"

Article Title: CJP launches website, invites proof against ‘police excesses’
Article Text:
CJP representatives appealed to protesters from across the country to submit visual evidence of the alleged assault.





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) Friday launched a dedicated website inviting protesters to upload photographs and videos of police personnel who allegedly assaulted demonstrators during and after the July 20 Sansad Chalo march, saying it would identify the officers and pursue legal action against them.Launching the portal at Jantar Mantar, CJP representatives appealed to protesters from across the country to submit visual evidence of the alleged assault.“We will go through every photograph and video, verify them, identify the police personnel involved and file complaints against them. We will demand registration of FIRs against such officers. If FIRs are not registered, we will approach the courts. Lawyers from across the country have come forward to help us and we will obtain court orders to ensure cases are registered,” CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said.He said the organisation will prepare a list of officers allegedly involved in the clampdown and “ensure they are punished till the end”.Besides reiterating its demand for action against the cops allegedly involved, CJP has also sought a public apology from the Delhi police commissioner, Rapid Action Force head and the Centre.“We request that all these demands be accepted at the earliest, failing which the movement will only grow bigger and spread across the country,” CJP said in a letter submitted to Centre Friday.It also sought an assurance that protesters would not be targeted in future, and said in-principal approval for this demand was given by Centre’s representatives who met the CJP spokespersons Friday.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) Friday launched a dedicated website inviting protesters to upload photographs and videos of police personnel who allegedly assaulted demonstrators during and after the Sansad Chalo march. CJP representatives appealed to protesters from across the country to submit visual evidence of the alleged assault.

NEW DELHI: Gitanjali J Angmo, Sonam Wangchuk 's wife, claimed the activist has been under constant vigil, saying "police are everywhere", be it at the reception, in the lifts or outside the ICU.She said the cops have been deciding who "may or may not meet him", questioning whether the authorities were defying the court's order on his detention."At both Safdarjung and now Medanta, police are everywhere. At the main gate. The reception. The lifts. Outside@Wangchuk66’s ICU. They decide who may or may not meet him. If the Court has clarified that he is not under detention, then under what authority is this happening?" Gitanjali wrote on X.She further wrote: "In an enlightened democracy, is the role of the police to protect citizens and uphold the law, or to control citizens on behalf of those in power? These are questions every Indian should be asking."Meanwhile, Sonam Wangchuk, hours after he ended his 26-day hunger strike in the presence of Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, said he made the decision only after he got assurances from the govt and MPs across party lines that his demands for exam reforms and no action against peaceful protesters would be met.In a video posted on X early Friday, Wangchuk said he extended his fast by two days as negotiations with the Centre were under way and he finally got a written assurance.“End of hunger... Beginning of accountability,” Wangchuk posted on X, sharing a video explaining his decision to end the hunger strike. “Negotiations were on for these assurances since the last two days, for which I had to extend my hunger strike. I could have extended it further if required,” he said.After Wangchuk broke his fast, Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke posted on X: “We are relieved and grateful that Sonam sir has ended his hunger strike after 26 days. Thank you, sir, for your extraordinary courage and sacrifice. By putting your own life on the line, you awakened the conscience of an entire nation. Your life is far too precious to this country. The Cockroach Janta Party’s peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar will continue until Dharmendra Pradhan resigns. ”Wangchuk said in his post that he ended the fast after getting assurance from the government and MPs of all political parties that the issue of accountability in the ‘failing’ examination system would be discussed in Parliament.The engineer and climate activist broke his fast with juice a little after 12.30 am Friday and followed it up with a bowl of chicken soup as part of the initial phase of nutritional rehabilitation, according to sources in Medanta.“After 26 days, this tastes very good, but hunger doesn’t taste bad either. My doctors here have been very, very kind,” he said from his hospital bed, surrounded by doctors, the ministers and his wife Gitanjali J Angmo.He said 65 MPs from different political parties had extended support to his campaign and that he insisted on a written commitment after two days of discussions with the Centre.“Both the ruling party and MPs from the opposition have assured me their discussions will happen on thefloor of Parliament regarding reforms in the examination system like NEET and others, and that we will also be discussing the accountability of such lapses. And that we will make sure such things never happen… You will take accountability in the ministry with the minister also as a responsibility, and I’m sure you are already considering.And with these assurances, I’m touched and grateful to govt, and I want to appeal to the protesting students to maintain utmost peace. To express their feelings is a legitimate thing, but I do not approve violence of any kind, and allowing any antisocial elements to take advantage of this is not acceptable to me. It should be a genuine demand by genuinely concerned people, in this case youngsters. Sowith that being fulfilled, I'm grateful and I'll be happy to break my fast,” he says in the video.
Article Summary: Gitanjali J Angmo, Sonam Wangchuk's wife, claimed the activist has been under constant vigil. She said the cops have been deciding who "may or may not meet him", questioning whether the authorities were defying the court's order on his detention.

Article Title: NATO-backed scientists planted 13-foot-tall giant grass on war-damaged land near Bucha, hoping its roots can help clean Ukraine's polluted soil
Article Text:
Scientists prepare a field for Miscanthus plants in northern Czech Republic (AFP photo)

Breadbasket of Europe

Testing giant Miscanthus

A Ukrainian fighter walks past a burning wheat field (Reuters file photo)

How grass helps soil

Improving soil naturally

A Ukrainian farmer watches as patches of his wheat fields burn (AP file photo)

Research underway in Ukraine

Early findings are encouraging

More than four years of war have left lasting damage across parts of Ukraine. It has not only affected buildings and infrastructure, but also the natural environment. Areas that once supported forests, wildlife and agriculture have been reduced to barren lands which could take years to recover.Ukraine's rich black soil has long been one of the country's biggest strengths. This natural asset helped the European nation become one of the world's leading producers and exporters of grain. Years of war have left it damaged and polluted, making farming difficult in some places.Researchers at the Jan Evangelista Purkyne University (UJEP) in the Czech Republic are testing giant Miscanthus, a fast-growing grass, to see if it can gradually remove harmful pollutants from contaminated soil while also producing biomass that can be used for energy.The research is part of a NATO-backed project that aims to reduce the environmental damage caused by military conflict. Scientists say the process is slow and could take years, but early findings suggest the grass may improve soil health and prepare damaged land for future farming.Ukraine is often called the 'breadbasket of Europe' because of its vast areas of chernozem or black soil. The soil is rich in nutrients and organic matter, making it one of the most fertile soils in the world.It has helped Ukraine become a major producer of wheat, maize and other crops.However, after nearly four-and-a-half years of war, large areas of farmland have been affected by military activity. Soil in some regions has been polluted by oil products, explosives and other contaminants.Heavy vehicles, shelling and fighting have also damaged the land by compacting the soil and destroying vegetation. Restoring this land will be essential if it is to be used for agriculture again.At an experimental site on a former brown coal mine near Most in northern Czech Republic, researchers are growing giant Miscanthus to understand how it behaves in damaged soil."The goal is to revitalise contaminated areas while producing biomass," UJEP environmental scientist Josef Trogl says, as quoted by news agency AFP.Giant Miscanthus is originally from East Asia but is now grown across Europe. It is mainly used as a biomass crop because its dried stems can be burned to produce heat and energy.Researchers believe the plant may also help clean polluted land through a natural process called phytoremediation.Scientists say the plant develops a large and deep root system. These roots can trap some harmful substances, including certain metals and other pollutants, while improving the condition of the soil.Ember Morrissey, a biologist at West Virginia University and co-author of a recent study on giant Miscanthus, says the grass is "capable of growing on degraded and contaminated soils and produces extensive root systems that can accumulate metals while simultaneously restoring soil organic matter."According to the researchers, most of the pollutants remain in the roots underground. The stems and leaves that grow above the ground stay largely clean and can still be harvested as biomass.The plant also improves soil quality in another important way. "The plant also sends up to 40% of organic material it produces through photosynthesis to the soil via its roots, which is way more than other farm plants," Trogl said.Photosynthesis is the process by which plants use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into food, releasing oxygen as a by-product. As giant Miscanthus grows, its deep roots store large amounts of carbon in the soil. Scientists say this helps restore soil organic matter and gradually improves soil health over time.Healthy soil contains organic matter called humus, which helps retain water and nutrients needed for plant growth. Trogl says giant Miscanthus encourages the formation of humus more effectively than many other crops."The development of humus and soil fertility is better here than under other plants," he said, adding that the grass also supports soil microorganisms to faster degrade organic pollutants such as petroleum.Soil microorganisms are tiny living organisms, including bacteria and fungi, that naturally break down harmful substances. By creating better conditions for these organisms, the plant may help speed up the recovery of contaminated land.The Czech research is not limited to laboratory testing. Since 2023, scientists have also been growing giant Miscanthus in Vorzel, near Bucha, a suburb of Kyiv.The area was occupied by Russian forces between February and March 2022 before being liberated the following month. It was later cleared of mines during autumn 2022.According to Valentina Pidlisnyuk, a Ukraine-born professor at UJEP who leads the research team, the land suffered extensive environmental damage."The area was occupied by Russian troops between February and March 2022, liberated in April 2022, and subsequently demined in autumn 2022," she said.Although the grass takes several years to show its full impact, scientists say the first results are positive. Pidlisnyuk said analyses carried out so far have shown positive effects on soil biological parameters and carbon sequestration.Carbon sequestration means capturing and storing carbon in the soil instead of releasing it into the atmosphere. This not only improves soil quality but can also help reduce the amount of carbon dioxide contributing to climate change.Researchers say the project is giving them valuable information about how damaged land can be restored using natural methods instead of relying only on expensive engineering solutions.Worth €346,000 (around $395,000), the project involves researchers from the Czech Republic, Ukraine, Canada, Croatia, Kazakhstan and the United States. It is currently scheduled to continue until next year.
Article Summary: Ukraine's rich black soil has long been one of the country's biggest strengths. Years of war have left it damaged and polluted, making farming difficult in some places. Scientists are testing giant Miscanthus, a fast-growing grass, to see if it can remove harmful pollutants from contaminated soil.

Article Title: Trump confirms Netanyahu's US visit next week amid regional tensions
Article Text:
Trump's remark came in his speech at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner on Friday.

United States President Donald Trump said that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will visit the US next week as the American forces continue to pound parts of Iran after peace talks fizzled out despite weeks of talks and signing of the MoU between Washington and Tehran.Trump's remark came in his speech at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner on Friday.Netanyahu and Trump agreed to meet in the United States a few weeks ago following a phone conversation. During the call, Netanyahu congratulated Trump on the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States and praised the close relationship between the two countries.It comes as the US-Israeli war with Iran has again escalated following a breakdown earlier this month of a ceasefire reached as part of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed by the US and Iran.Israel had opposed the agreement from the outset, while its continuing military operations in Lebanon repeatedly threatened diplomatic efforts in the region.The Trump administration has also been mediating separate talks between Israel and Lebanon aimed at ending hostilities. The negotiations do not involve Hezbollah.Both sides have accepted a proposal under which Israeli-held areas in southern Lebanon would eventually be handed over to the Lebanese military.However, there has been little visible progress on the ground since March.During a meeting with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun earlier this week, Trump did not indicate when Israeli forces would withdraw from the occupied areas.Meanwhile, the US military said its Central Command had completed a 13th straight night of strikes against targets in Iran.Iran has continued to respond with attacks on US military assets across the region. Last week, a strike on a US base in Jordan killed three American soldiers.The United States has also increased its military deployment in Israel, a move that some analysts believe could signal preparations for a wider regional escalation.Netanyahu's visit will also take place as Israel's military campaign in Gaza continues. Despite a US-backed ceasefire announced last October, Israeli forces have continued issuing evacuation orders and carrying out frequent strikes across the territory.
Article Summary: Netanyahu and Trump agreed to meet in the United States a few weeks ago following a phone conversation. It comes as the US-Israeli war with Iran has again escalated following a breakdown earlier this month of a ceasefire reached as part of a Memorandum of Understanding.
